_note: Rationale registry for the mid-2030s profiles (mid2030s_low / mid2030s / mid2030s_high). These are SCENARIOS for a design study of a 2035 data centre, not forecasts: 'low' = slow progress, 'base' = default, 'high' = fast progress. The numbers themselves live in modalities.json, fridges.json and classical.json; this file records the anchors (with how well each was verified in the October 2026 audit), what was extrapolated, and the biggest uncertainty per group. Nothing here is a vendor commitment.

verification_levels.confirmed: read in a primary or vendor source
verification_levels.company_target: a roadmap goal, not a delivered result
verification_levels.unverified: from memory or not found in the audit

anchors.fact: Google Willow: below-threshold surface code, Lambda about 2.14 (d=3,5,7), distance 7 logical error 0.143 % per cycle
IBM Nighthawk 120 qubits and Loon (Nov 2025); Starling 2029: 200 logical qubits / 1e8 gates; Blue Jay 2033+: 2,000 logical / 1e9 gates

superconducting_qubits.biggest_uncertainty: whether two-qubit error reaches 3e-4 at scale and whether long-range couplers (qLDPC) work; the error-correction overhead scales steeply with Lambda.

anchors.fact: Bluefors KIDE: >1,000 qubits, >4,000 RF lines, >3,000 uW at 100 mK, three cooling units, nine pulse tubes
KIDE about 6 W at 4 K
anchors.level: unverified (modelling paper arXiv:2608.00990, page too large to fetch)

anchors.fact: Fermilab 'Colossus'-class platform

cryogenics_and_control.biggest_uncertainty: the 4 K and mixing-chamber heat budgets of 1e5-1e6 qubits: the wiring wall may simply cap one-fridge qubit counts (see the sweep command); cryoplant efficiency is an assumption.

anchors.fact: Helios: 98 qubits, 2-qubit 99.921 %, <40 kW base unit without support infrastructure
about 60 kW excluding HVAC in the Oracle announcement
Quantinuum Apollo 2029 (universal fault tolerant); IonQ 2M physical / up to 80,000 logical by 2030

trapped_ions.biggest_uncertainty: power per qubit once optics are integrated; gate speed (tens of microseconds) keeps logical clocks in the kHz range.

anchors.fact: QuEra Aquila 6.92 kW + 0.308 W/qubit (PaQit fit)
Pasqal laser 3.5 kW average / 10 kW installed
Pasqal 10,000+ physical / 200+ logical by about 2029-30; QuEra >256 logical, 1e-6 by 2028; Atom Computing AC1000 (1,200+ qubits), 50 logical qubits planned early 2027

neutral_atoms.biggest_uncertainty: how laser power and cameras scale beyond 1e4 atoms; millisecond cycles make Toffoli-heavy jobs take days.

anchors.fact: AWS Ocelot (Nature 2025): d=5 repetition code, 5 cat + 4 ancilla qubits, phase flip 27-33 us, bit flip >1 ms, logical error about 1.7 % per cycle (flat in d)
Gouzien et al. PRL 131, 040602: 126,133 cat qubits, 256-bit ECDLP in 9 h under optimistic assumptions
Alice & Bob: 100 logical qubits from about 2,000 cat qubits at 1e-6 by 2030

cat_qubits.biggest_uncertainty: the code itself (threshold, factory cost, outer code) and whether bit flips can be pushed below 1e-15 per cycle; the model is coarse.

anchors.fact: Quandela Ascella 6 qubits 3 kW incl. built-in cryostat
Quandela roadmap: <500 kW at hundreds of logical qubits (hybrid emitter scheme)
PsiQuantum Omega chipset, cryogenic cabinets, sites in Brisbane and Chicago; no power figure found

photonics.biggest_uncertainty: the whole overhead model (6 d^2 generators per logical qubit and a 1 us layer clock are assumptions); photonics could be an order of magnitude better or worse.

anchors.fact: B200 1.0 kW, H200 up to 700 W, MI355X up to 1.4 kW, DGX B200 14.3 kW max
Rubin about 1.8 kW per board (Igor's Lab) or 2.3 kW per GPU (analyst), 288 GB HBM4, 22 TB/s
Rubin Ultra / Kyber NVL576 rack about 600 kW, 2H 2027 (Jensen Huang, GTC; Data Center Dynamics)
Google: >500 kW per rack by 2030; Mt Diablo / NVIDIA 800 VDC up to 1 MW racks
KAIST TERALAB hypothetical HBM roadmap: HBM4 about 75 W/stack, HBM5 about 100-120 W, HBM8 180 W, ~8 TB/s HBM6, ~24 TB/s HBM7 (about 2035)

gpus_and_memory.biggest_uncertainty: whether module power keeps rising (cooling-limited) and how much of the efficiency gain is delivered at the application level; LLM tokens/s per module follows memory bandwidth in this model.

anchors.fact: D-Wave Advantage2: more than 4,400 qubits, average power 12.5 kW, constant over six generations (vendor claim)

annealers.biggest_uncertainty: time-to-target on real problem classes against strong classical solvers: nothing in the model asserts an advantage.
